source_text: Early stopping rules, applied after interim analyses at approximately 20–30% of planned enrollment, have drawn scrutiny for potentially overstating efficacy, as such decisions amplify type I errors and may capture transient effects not sustained long-term; for instance, the Auvert trial halted after 1,200 infections despite a planned sample exceeding 3,000. [100]
